instruction.text: Select the two things that need to happen before an animal is born.

feedback.end: To understand how fertilisation and growth take place, let’s look at reproduction among humans.
Fertilisation happens when a male’s sperm and a female’s egg join together.
The male’s sperm fertilises the female’s egg. The offspring receives half of its genes from each parent. This happens among all animals that carry out sexual reproduction.

atoms.b: After fertilisation, the future offspring is ready to start ((++growing shrinking)).
First, the fertilised egg multiplies into a tiny cluster of cells known as an ((++embryo baby)).
After around 9 weeks, the embryo develops into a foetus and begins to grow organs and ((++body_parts trees)). This all takes place inside the body of the ((++female male)).
After around 9 months of growth, the baby is ready to be born and start life ((++outside inside)) the mother’s body.

instruction.text: Select the correct stage of human reproduction.

atoms.b: Other mammals grow their babies in the same way as humans. The developing babies of mammals are kept ((++inside underneath)) the female’s body.
This is known as ((++gestation digestion)). The gestation period is the time between fertilisation and ((++birth death)).
Inside the female’s body, the babies of wild animals are better protected from dangers like ((++predators prey)). They also receive oxygen and ((++nutrients sweets)) from their mother.
